title: AHB Address and Control Signals
description: Select an AHB address-phase signal to see exact base encodings, optional AHB5 property gates, accepted-edge sampling, and pending-transfer stability. The selected IHI 0011A and IHI 0033B.b base interfaces use HADDR[31:0].

signals.name: HADDR[31:0]
signals.description: Identifies the byte address in the system address map for the visible address phase.
signals.direction: Master → decoder, interconnect, and selected slave
signals.sampled: Accepted on a rising HCLK edge only when HREADY is HIGH and HTRANS[1] is HIGH
values: Aligned to 2^HSIZE for a valid transfer
signals.verificationNote: For a pending NONSEQ/SEQ transfer during an ordinary OKAY wait, hold HADDR and its complete address context stable; model the protocol-defined IDLE, BUSY, and first-ERROR-cycle exceptions.

signals.name: HWRITE
signals.description: Selects write data from the master or read data from the slave for the accepted transfer.
signals.verificationNote: Capture HWRITE into data-phase context; current visible HWRITE belongs to the next address phase and cannot classify stalled HWDATA.

signals.name: HSIZE
signals.description: Encodes 2^HSIZE bytes for each transfer beat and therefore the sequential address increment.
signals.verificationNote: An encoding is legal only when its transfer size does not exceed the implemented data-bus width and HADDR is naturally aligned.

signals.name: HBURST
signals.description: Declares whether the transfer is single, incrementing, or wrapping and gives fixed beat count where applicable.
signals.sampled: At the first beat and stable across the burst
signals.verificationNote: A mid-burst HBURST change is a protocol violation.

signals.name: HTRANS
signals.description: Describes the current visible address phase: IDLE, BUSY, first valid beat, or continuing valid beat.
signals.sampled: A NONSEQ/SEQ beat is accepted only on a rising HCLK edge with HREADY HIGH
signals.verificationNote: Only accepted NONSEQ/SEQ values consume beats. BUSY preserves eligible burst context but is not a transfer and does not itself retain arbitration ownership.

signals.name: HPROT[3:0]
signals.description: Describes instruction/data, user/privileged, bufferable, and cacheable attributes. AHB carries attributes; the system's configured enforcement point defines access policy.
signals.direction: Master → decoder, interconnect, and selected slave
signals.verificationNote: Check attribute propagation and the documented policy response; AHB does not universally require every target to reject every privilege mismatch.

signals.name: HPROT[6:4]
signals.description: Present only when the Extended_Memory_Types interface property is declared; extends memory-type information without changing base HPROT[3:0].
signals.sampled: With the accepted address phase and held with its pending context
values: Property present: Normal/Device memory attributes per IHI 0033B.b
signals.verificationNote: Gate signal presence, stimulus, checking, and coverage by the declared property.

signals.name: HNONSEC
signals.description: Present only when Secure_Transfers is declared and identifies Secure or Non-secure address-phase attribution.
signals.direction: Master → configured routing and enforcement points
signals.sampled: Same validity and stability constraints as HADDR
signals.verificationNote: Check attribution propagation and configured enforcement; security policy is not equivalent to locking or exclusive access.

signals.name: HEXCL / HMASTER
signals.expansion: Optional AHB5 exclusive request and identity
signals.description: Present for the Exclusive_Transfers property. HEXCL identifies an exclusive address phase; HMASTER supplies monitor identity.
signals.direction: Master/interconnect → exclusive monitor and selected slave
signals.sampled: With a valid NONSEQ exclusive address phase
signals.verificationNote: Gate by configuration and check the complete matching attribute set; an exclusive is conditional, not a bus reservation.

signals.name: HMASTLOCK
signals.description: Identifies transfers in a locked sequence. Original shared AHB distinguishes a master's HLOCKx request from arbiter-generated bus-level HMASTLOCK; AHB-Lite/AHB5 still define HMASTLOCK.
signals.direction: Original arbiter or AHB-Lite/AHB5 manager/interconnect → selected target path
signals.sampled: With the address phase for the locked sequence
signals.verificationNote: Check active ownership is not transferred within the applicable locked arbitration/resource path. Fairness outside the sequence is a separate product contract.
